draftBefore.emotion: matter-of-fact and direct, describing the current state of things
notes: Haben is the most common verb in German to show possession. It is also used as an auxiliary verb to form the perfect tense for most other verbs, similar to 'have' in English.

Do not confuse 'haben' (to have) with 'es gibt' (there is/there are). Use 'haben' when a specific subject owns or possesses something, and 'es gibt' when you are merely stating that something exists in a location.
